blockers.summary: Release blocked by SRU team (block-proposed-noble)

autopkgtest failure/regression reported: "…e StableReleaseUpdates policy regarding autopkgtest regressions [1]. https://ubuntu-archive-team.ubuntu.com/proposed-migration/noble/updat…" (ubuntu-sru-bot)
Regression mentioned: "…Potential regression: libvirt RBD storage pools on noble Upstream Ceph 19.2.6 removed the deprecate…" (mstevens-imt-systems)
Regression mentioned: "…d-party software involved. So this is a regression for any noble host using libvirt RBD storage pools, not just CloudStack. Note…" (mstevens-imt-systems)
Regression mentioned: "…ne already spoken up and called out the regression that this upload would introduce. On the libvirt side this is reported and trac…" (paelzer)
Regression mentioned: "…Added the tested with a regression test in CI. Test: https://github.com/canonical/ceph-charms/pull/220/changes/2…" (johnramsden)

The 19.2.6 package in noble-proposed (0ubuntu0.24.04.1) drops the `auth_supported` option, which breaks libvirt RBD storage pools ("failed to set RADOS option: auth_supported"). The fix is only in a PPA (.2), not yet uploaded to noble-proposed, and the SRU team has been asked to keep the package in proposed.

The fix relies on the libvirt fix (LP: #2172324). Ceph must either carry the `auth_supported` compat patch or declare Breaks/Conflicts against older libvirt, so users who upgrade one package but not the other are not regressed. Neither is settled.

Release-order dependency: 19.2.6 contains the CephX CVE fix and must not ship until 20.2.4 (LP: #2166817) is released in resolute and stonking. Otherwise users upgrading to an unpatched 20.x would hit authentication failures. The 20.2.4 upload was still unapproved in resolute at last report.

The noble autopkgtest regression in libvirt (arm64) triggered by the ceph upload has no documented resolution. It is likely related to the auth_supported removal, and has not been shown to be fixed or acceptably retried.

Existing verification-done tags and the CI test results (ceph-charms run) predate the respin that restores `auth_supported`. The respun package (.2) needs re-verification in -proposed, and the tags are inconsistent with the block-proposed-noble tag.
The kernel-related implications of the CephX CVE change (client compatibility, communication to users) were still undecided. This may need release notes or other handling before release.

comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html

Are they just lacking reviews in the mailing list? Or are there other concerns?
